title: FIBS-enabled Noninvasive Metabolic Profiling
protocol: Revive CHO cells in 9 ml CD-CHO medium supplemented with 8 mM L-Glutamine and 10 ml/L hypoxanthine/thymidine supplement.
Centrifuge the revived cells at 100 x g for 5 min.
Resuspend the cells in 10 ml of fresh complete growth medium.
Remove a 1 ml sample and determine the viable cell concentration by light microscopy using the trypan blue dye exclusion method in a hemocytometer.
Initiate a culture at a seeding density of 3 x 10^5 cells/ml in 125 ml shake flasks.
Maintain the culture in an incubator at 37 °C, with a humidified atmosphere of 5% CO2, on an orbital shaking platform rotating at 120 rpm.
Subculture every 3-4 days in complete growth medium at a seeding density of 2 x 10^5 cells/ml.
Prepare plasmid DNA using a large-scale plasmid purification kit.
Maintain cells at the appropriate conditions (37 °C, 5% CO2) for 12-24 hr prior to transfection.
Count the cells using the trypan blue dye exclusion method.
Prepare a working volume of 20 ml of cell culture in a 125 ml shake flask at a concentration of 1 x 10^6 cells/ml.
Use a suitable transfection kit for the cell line in use.
Mix plasmid DNA and transfection reagents according to the manufacturer's guidelines and the specific requirements of the cell line.
Incubate the cells for 4 days in static mode.
Transfer the cultures to a shaking platform rotating at 125 rpm.
Add an appropriate antibiotic, such as zeocin, to a final concentration of 400 μg/ml for plasmid selection.
Change media and add antibiotic at intervals suitable for the cell line until control wells are depleted.
Select the most confluent wells for further experiments.
Establish a cell bank by freezing cells in cryogenic vials containing 10^7 viable cells in 1 ml of freeze mix.
Maintain the freeze mix composition as 92.5% growth medium and 7.5% dimethyl sulfoxide.
Follow instructions for cell maintenance to establish triplicate cell cultures in 250 ml shake flasks with a working volume of 50 ml.
Maintain cultures in a humidified cell incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Rotate cultures on an orbital shaking platform at 125 rpm.
Remove 4.1 ml samples from each culture at 24-hour intervals.
Use 100 μl of the sample to determine viable cell concentration and viability using trypan blue dye exclusion method.
Repeat sampling until viable cell concentration is reduced to zero.
Supplement fed-batch cultures with appropriate amount of glucose or glutamine on day 6 to restore concentrations to initial values (36 mM for glucose, 4 mM for glutamine).
Maintain additional control cultures by feeding them with the same volume of pure water as experimental cultures.
Take 2 ml daily samples removed from cultures and centrifuge at 100 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Resuspend cell pellet in 2 ml ice cold phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Transfer resuspended cells into a 6-well plate, including a blank sample with no cells in one well.
Measure blue fluorescence at an excitation wavelength of 430/435 nm and emission wavelength of 465/435 nm.
Measure yellow fluorescence at an excitation wavelength of 430/435 nm and emission wavelength of 520/510 nm.
Calculate FRET ratios by dividing the level of yellow fluorescence by blue fluorescence detected.
Take 2 ml daily samples removed from cultures and centrifuge at 100 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Remove supernatant to perform metabolite assays.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 3 ml ice cold PBS.
Centrifuge at 100 x g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 3 ml ice cold PBS.
Sonicate the sample 5x for 3 min each with a pulse of 15 sec on and 15 sec off.
Construct a standard curve using appropriate standards for glucose ranging between 0-100 mM.
Use an appropriate glucose assay kit to determine the intracellular glucose concentration following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Calculate the glucose concentrations using the linear equation y = 1310.51x - 723.43, where y is absorbance reading and x is glucose concentration.
Take dilution into account when calculating the glucose concentrations.
Use an appropriate glutamine assay kit to determine the intracellular glutamine concentration following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Construct a standard curve using appropriate standards for glutamine ranging between 0-2 mM.
Construct a calibration curve using the equation y = 203.1x + 17.1, where y is the absorbance reading and x is the glucose concentration.
Calculate the glutamine concentration of the samples using the standard curve.
Adjust the calculated glutamine concentrations for dilution factors applied to the samples.
Use Equation 1 to calculate the intracellular glutamine concentration.
